items.title: Charlie De Vore Interview, 1962-07-04
items.q: I went over to Johnny Wig's house every Sunday afternoon for about three or four months, and all he did was just show me chords.

ctx.x: I'm Dick Allen. Okay, what are we going to talk about today? How to learn how to play New Orleans jazz and how to set up a school, we hope, some sort of thing where we can have seminars and private lessons or what have you, and set up a band. What are your ideas on this, Charlie? You've had some experience.

Well, I don't know exactly what you want, but... Neither do we. If you're just interested in the band aspect as opposed against the individual aspect, there's a few simple little things that can be done to make it pretty fundamental. Now, I think, from my own experience anyway, you've got to have one or two guys with fairly sharp ears if you're going to learn the various tunes. And for musicians that aren't from New Orleans and haven't heard the tunes, the only way they can pick them up is from records, of…
